prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Customer Onboarding Field Validation Rules (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Field" · longest unbreakable word 141px · one-line width 141px
  col 2: header "Pattern" · longest unbreakable word 129px · one-line width 1217px
  col 3: header "Example valid" · longest unbreakable word 185px · one-line width 293px
  col 4: header "Error message" · longest unbreakable word 174px · one-line width 777px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 788px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 787px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 788px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A reference table for onboarding engineers and support staff to validate customer input fields: each row names a field, gives its regex rule, a valid sample, and the user-facing error text.","reading":"Readers scan row by row, using Field as the anchor, then inspect Pattern and check Example valid / Error message. Pattern is the longest technical content and will wrap regardless; error messages are prose and can wrap naturally; field names and sample values should remain recognizable tokens.","groups":["Field + Example valid: concrete input identity; keep adjacent so a reader can confirm what the field accepts.","Pattern + Error message: validation rule and its diagnostic; both explain why an input passes or fails."],"keep_intact":["Field identifiers such as account_email, phone_e164, postal_code_us","Regex unbreakable tokens and character classes, especially the longest ~129px token","Example valid values such as email addresses, phone numbers, dates, amounts, slugs and VAT IDs","Header words; avoid mid-word breaks"],"may_wrap":["Error message prose at word boundaries","Pattern at safe punctuation or group boundaries between intact regex tokens","Example valid only when unavoidable, preferably at natural separators"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[162,224,206,195],"idea":"Keep Field, Example valid and Error message at their integrity minimums and give all spare width to Pattern, accepting tall regex rows to maximize rule readability."},{"name":"B","widths":[162,180,250,195],"idea":"Trim Pattern to a workable wrap width and spend the surplus on Example valid so concrete samples stay closer to one line and are easier to compare."},{"name":"C","widths":[162,180,206,239],"idea":"Keep Pattern merely workable and widen Error message so the diagnostic prose reads in fewer, more natural lines for support and troubleshooting."}]}
